Use list_game_data_sheets to discover names and get_game_data_sheet_info to see which columns are searchable.

Parameters:

tools.name: get_territory

Looks up a zone/territory by id or name: name, region, zone, map, whether it is a PvP zone, and whether mounts are allowed.

tools.name: get_class_job

Class and job definitions. Omit classJobId to list every class and job with its abbreviation, which is the cheapest way to map a job id to a name.

tools.name: read_memory
tools.title: Read memory
tools.description:
Reads raw process memory at an absolute address. Use format=hexdump for a classic hex+ASCII view of a struct, or a scalar format (u8/u16/u32/u64/i8..i64/f32/f64/pointer/bool/string/utf16) to decode one value. Addresses are validated against the OS region map before reading, so an unmapped or no-access address returns an error rather than crashing the game. Pass the address as a hex string such as "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4" to avoid JSON number precision loss.

Parameters:
  - address (string): Absolute address, e.g. "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4"
  - length (integer): Bytes to read. Defaults to 256 for hexdump, 1024 for string, else the format's size.
  - format (string (hexdump | bytes | u8 | u16 | u32 | u64 | i8 | i16 | i32 | i64 | f32 | f64 | bool | string | utf16 | pointer)): How to decode the bytes (default hexdump)

length.description: Bytes to read. Defaults to 256 for hexdump, 1024 for string, else the format's size.

format.description: How to decode the bytes (default hexdump)

tools.name: query_memory_region
tools.title: Query memory region
tools.description:
Describes what the OS reports for one or more addresses: whether the page is committed, readable, writable, executable, its protection flags, and which allocation region it belongs to. Use this to understand a struct layout before reading it, or to find out why a read failed.

Parameters:
  - address (string): Absolute address to describe, e.g. "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4"
  - length (integer): Also report every region spanning this many bytes from the address

length.description: Also report every region spanning this many bytes from the address

tools.name: read_pointer_chain
tools.title: Read pointer chain
tools.description:
Follows a multi-level pointer: dereferences a pointer at the base address, adds the first offset, dereferences again, and so on, then optionally reads a value at the final address. This is the standard way to reach a single field from a static base. Returns every intermediate address so a broken step is obvious.

Parameters:
  - address (string): Base address to start from, e.g. "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4"
  - offsets (array): Offsets applied after each dereference, one per level. JSON has no hex literals, so pass hex as a string: [16, 448] and ["0x10", "0x1C0"] both work.
  - valueFormat (string): Optional: also decode a value at the final address (same names as read_memory)

address.description: Base address to start from, e.g. "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4"

offsets.description: Offsets applied after each dereference, one per level. JSON has no hex literals, so pass hex as a string: [16, 448] and ["0x10", "0x1C0"] both work.

valueFormat.description: Optional: also decode a value at the final address (same names as read_memory)

tools.name: get_module_info
tools.title: Get module info
tools.description: The game module's load address and its .text / .data / .rdata section bases and sizes. Combine a section base with an offset to get an absolute address for read_memory. Every address is returned as a hex string.

tools.name: scan_signature
tools.title: Scan signature
tools.description:
Scans the game's code or data for a byte pattern with wildcards, using Dalamud's signature scanner. Patterns look like "48 8B 05 ?? ?? ?? ?? 48 85 C0" where ?? matches any byte. Use this to locate a function or global that has no stable offset, then read_memory the address it returns.

Parameters:
  - signature (string): Byte pattern with ?? wildcards, e.g. "48 8B 05 ?? ?? ?? ??"
  - maxResults (integer): Maximum matches to return (default 1, use 0 for all)
  - section (string (text | data | rdata | module)): Which section to scan (default text)

maxResults.description: Maximum matches to return (default 1, use 0 for all)

tools.name: read_object_memory
tools.title: Read object memory
tools.description:
Reads memory at a game object's address plus an offset. Resolve the object by entityId, objectIndex, or localPlayer, then look at a specific field. This is the bridge between the typed object tools and raw memory: get_game_objects reports an object's address, and this reads the bytes behind it.

Parameters:
  - entityId (integer): Object entity id (from get_game_objects)
  - objectIndex (integer): Object table index
  - localPlayer (boolean): Read from the local player's object address
  - address (string): Read from this absolute object address instead of resolving one
  - offset (integer): Byte offset from the object's base address (default 0)
  - length (integer): Bytes to read (default 64)
  - format (string (hexdump | bytes | u8 | u16 | u32 | u64 | i8 | i16 | i32 | i64 | f32 | f64 | bool | string | utf16 | pointer)): How to decode the bytes (default hexdump)

localPlayer.description: Read from the local player's object address

address.description: Read from this absolute object address instead of resolving one

offset.description: Byte offset from the object's base address (default 0)

format.description: How to decode the bytes (default hexdump)

tools.name: get_job_gauge
tools.title: Get job gauge
tools.description: Reads the current job gauge straight out of FFXIVClientStructs' JobGaugeManager: the job's ClassJobId and every field of that job's gauge struct, including named bit fields. This is the only gauge surface the plugin has - Dalamud's managed job-gauge accessor is not one of the services it is given. Reports available=false with a reason when the client is not running or its signatures have not resolved.

tools.name: get_active_statuses
tools.title: Get active statuses
tools.description:
Reads a character's StatusManager directly out of FFXIVClientStructs: the status array (id, parameter, remaining time, source) plus the header fields Dalamud's managed status list does not expose - the manager's owner, its flag byte, and the special-status timer. Names come from the Status sheet. Identify the character with address, entityId, objectIndex, or localPlayer.

Parameters:
  - address (string): Raw address of the object as a hex string, e.g. "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4"
  - entityId (integer): Entity id of an object in the object table
  - objectIndex (integer): Index into the object table
  - localPlayer (boolean): Read the local player's statuses (equivalent to entityId of the local player)
  - max (integer): Maximum statuses to return (default 60, which is the full array)

address.description: Raw address of the object as a hex string, e.g. "0x7FF6A1B2C3D4"

entityId.description: Entity id of an object in the object table

localPlayer.description: Read the local player's statuses (equivalent to entityId of the local player)

max.description: Maximum statuses to return (default 60, which is the full array)

tools.name: open_addon
tools.title: Open an addon (UI window)
tools.description:
Opens one of the game's addon (UI window) surfaces the way its own keyboard shortcut would: through the FFXIVClientStructs agent layer (AgentInterface.Show). Bounded to an allowlist of standalone-openable system windows; anything that must be opened from a parent context is refused by design. This is a mutating tool: it is hidden from tools/list and refused by tools/call while the plugin's allow-mutating-tools switch is off.

Parameters:
  - addon (string (achievement | actionmenu | adventurenotebook | aethercurrent | aquarium | armoury | blacklist | cabinet | characterconfig | chatconfig | chocobobreed | chocoborace | colorant | companions | config | contacts | contentsnote | currency | deepdungeonmap | deepdungeonstatus | dutyfinder | emote | fishguide | fishingnote | freecompany | freecompanychest | freecompanyprofile | friendlist | gatheringnote | gearsets | goldsaucer | howto | hudlayout | inventory | itemdetail | itemsearch | journaldetail | keybindconfig | legacyitemstorage | letter | licenseviewer | linkshell | lookingforparty | materiaattach | materialize | minionnotebook | mirageprism | monsternote | mountnotebook | orchestrion | partysearch | playguide | pvpprofile | questjournal | raidfinder | recipenote | relicnotebook | repair | retainer | salvage | screenlog | social | teleport | tripletriad | weatherreport | weblauncher)): Which addon to open.

tools.name: close_addon
tools.title: Close an addon (UI window)
tools.description:
Closes one of the game's addon (UI window) surfaces through the agent layer (AgentInterface.Hide), the same path the game's own close action takes. Accepts the same allowlist names as open_addon. This is a mutating tool: it is hidden from tools/list and refused by tools/call while the plugin's allow-mutating-tools switch is off.

Parameters:
  - addon (string (achievement | actionmenu | adventurenotebook | aethercurrent | aquarium | armoury | blacklist | cabinet | characterconfig | chatconfig | chocobobreed | chocoborace | colorant | companions | config | contacts | contentsnote | currency | deepdungeonmap | deepdungeonstatus | dutyfinder | emote | fishguide | fishingnote | freecompany | freecompanychest | freecompanyprofile | friendlist | gatheringnote | gearsets | goldsaucer | howto | hudlayout | inventory | itemdetail | itemsearch | journaldetail | keybindconfig | legacyitemstorage | letter | licenseviewer | linkshell | lookingforparty | materiaattach | materialize | minionnotebook | mirageprism | monsternote | mountnotebook | orchestrion | partysearch | playguide | pvpprofile | questjournal | raidfinder | recipenote | relicnotebook | repair | retainer | salvage | screenlog | social | teleport | tripletriad | weatherreport | weblauncher)): Which addon to close.

tools.name: get_addon_state
tools.title: Get addon (UI window) state
tools.description: Reports which of the allowlisted addon surfaces the agent layer currently considers active (its window open), keyed by the same names open_addon accepts. Read-only.

tools.name: list_addon_elements
tools.title: List addon (UI window) elements
tools.description:
Walks a loaded addon's UI node tree and reports its clickable elements: node id, type, label text, screen rectangle, and visible/enabled state. Pass 'addon' as a name from get_addon_state's allowlist, or 'addonId' as the raw AtkUnitBase id. Use the returned nodeId with click_addon_element. Read-only.

Parameters:
  - addon (string): Addon name to inspect (same names open_addon accepts)
  - addonId (integer): Raw AtkUnitBase id of the addon to inspect (overrides addon)
  - maxDepth (integer): Maximum node-tree depth to walk (default 12)
  - maxNodes (integer): Maximum elements to report (default 100)
  - allNodes (boolean): Report every node, not just labeled/clickable ones (default false)

addon.description: Addon name to inspect (same names open_addon accepts)

addonId.description: Raw AtkUnitBase id of the addon to inspect (overrides addon)

allNodes.description: Report every node, not just labeled/clickable ones (default false)

tools.name: click_addon_element
tools.title: Click an addon (UI window) element
tools.description:
Dispatches one UI event (default: left click) at a node inside a loaded addon, through the addon's own event pipeline — the same dispatch a real mouse click feeds it. Resolve a nodeId with list_addon_elements first. For list components you may pass 'index' to click a list item directly. This is a mutating tool: it is hidden from tools/list and refused by tools/call while the plugin's allow-mutating-tools switch is off.

Parameters:
  - addon (string): Addon name to click inside (same names open_addon accepts)
  - addonId (integer): Raw AtkUnitBase id of the addon to click inside (overrides addon)
  - nodeId (integer): Target node id from list_addon_elements
  - index (integer): For list components: the item index to click instead of a nodeId
  - event (string): Which event to dispatch: click (default), doubleClick, buttonClick, buttonPress, buttonRelease, or 'registered' to fire every handler the node has registered (closest to a real mouse click)
  - param (integer): Override the event callback param (uint32). Advanced: the game normally derives it from the node's registered handler; ClickLib-style close buttons need 0xFFFFFFFF (-1)

tools.name: get_addon_strings
tools.title: Read an addon (UI window)'s value table
tools.description:
Reports the string and scalar values an addon currently carries in its AtkValue table — the text a menu, dialog or list is displaying right now. Each entry is index, type and decoded value; control characters are escaped so the raw payload is visible. Pass 'addon' or 'addonId'. Read-only.

Parameters:
  - addon (string): Addon name to read (same names open_addon accepts)
  - addonId (integer): Raw AtkUnitBase id to read (overrides addon)
  - maxValues (integer): Maximum entries to report (1-500, default 200)
  - stringsOnly (boolean): Only report string-typed values (default false)

addon.description: Addon name to read (same names open_addon accepts)

tools.name: select_addon_menu_item
tools.title: Select an item in an addon (UI window) menu
tools.description:
Picks an entry from a menu-style addon (one whose options live in its AtkValue table) by label, and activates it by firing the addon's callback with the entry's index — the same call the game makes when the option is clicked. Matching is exact after normalization unless containsMatch is set. Pass 'index' instead of 'label' to select positionally. Read the candidates first with get_addon_strings. This is a mutating tool: it is hidden from tools/list and refused by tools/call while the plugin's allow-mutating-tools switch is off.

Parameters:
  - addon (string): Addon name whose menu to select from
  - addonId (integer): Raw AtkUnitBase id (overrides addon)
  - label (string): Menu entry label to select (required unless index is given)
  - index (integer): Select by position instead of label
  - containsMatch (boolean): Match labels by substring instead of exact (default false)
  - dryRun (boolean): Report the entry that would be selected without activating it

Temporary diagnostic: swaps the ReceiveEvent vtable slot of one loaded addon so every UI event it receives (real mouse clicks and synthetic dispatches alike) is captured before being forwarded. Pass 'addon' (any loaded addon name) or 'addonId'. Use probe_receive_event_dump to read captures. Mutating.

Parameters:
  - addon (string): Addon name to hook (raw loaded addon name, e.g. Currency)
  - addonId (integer): Raw AtkUnitBase id of the addon to hook (overrides addon)

  - nodeId (integer): Node whose first registered listener should be hooked

tools.name: probe_receive_event_dump
tools.title: Dump captured ReceiveEvent calls (diagnostic)
tools.description: Returns every ReceiveEvent invocation captured since the hook was enabled: event type, param, and the raw event / event-data buffers decoded at their FCS offsets. Read-only.

tools.name: probe_callback_enable
tools.title: Hook the global FireCallback (diagnostic)
tools.description: Temporary diagnostic: installs a global hook on AtkUnitBase.FireCallback so every addon callback the game performs is recorded with its decoded AtkValue[] arguments — the same data SimpleTweaks' Addon Logging → Callbacks shows. Real UI interactions (button clicks, list picks) funnel into these callbacks, so the capture tells an agent exactly which (addon, values) payload reproduces an action. Use probe_callback_dump to read captures. Mutating.

tools.name: probe_callback_disable
tools.title: Unhook the FireCallback probe (diagnostic)
tools.description: Removes the global FireCallback hook installed by probe_callback_enable. Mutating.

tools.name: probe_callback_dump
tools.title: Dump captured FireCallback calls (diagnostic)
tools.description: Returns every addon callback captured since probe_callback_enable: addon name, value count, each AtkValue decoded by type (Int/UInt/Bool/String/...), the close/update-visibility flag, and the return value. Read-only.

tools.name: get_inventory
tools.title: Get inventory
tools.description: Items in the four player inventory bags (saddlebag and retainer bags are not included). Each entry: itemId, name, quantity, isHq, slot.

tools.name: get_equipment
tools.title: Get equipment
tools.description: Currently equipped gear with item level, condition/perfection, spiritbond, glamour id and materia count.

tools.name: get_buddy_list
tools.title: Get buddy list
tools.description: Companion (chocobo), pet and trust buddies currently following the player, with HP, level and stance where available.

tools.name: get_duty_state
tools.title: Get duty state
tools.description: Whether a duty (dungeon, raid, trial, etc.) is currently running, plus its content finder name when known.

tools.name: execute_action
tools.title: Execute action
tools.description:
Casts a job/general action by id, optionally by action name resolved from the Action sheet. Uses the normal UseAction path, so cooldowns, cast times and range checks all apply. Pass dryRun to ask whether the action could be used right now without using it.

Parameters:
  - actionId (integer): Action row id
  - actionName (string): Exact action sheet name; resolved to an id
  - targetObjectId (integer): Target game object id (defaults to self)
  - dryRun (boolean): Check usability instead of using the action

tools.name: plugin_data_subscribe

tools.description:
Retains the payloads a plugin pushes over the push channel under one key, in a dedicated queue that plugin_data_poll drains incrementally. Payloads that arrive while nothing is subscribed are only visible through query_push_data and are lost to the rolling buffer once it wraps.

Parameters:
  - key (string): Push-channel key (tag) to retain
  - capacity (integer): Retained entries before the oldest are dropped (16-10000, default 1000)

tools.name: plugin_data_poll
tools.title: Poll subscribed plugin data
tools.description:
Drains retained payloads for a subscribed key, oldest first. Drained entries are removed, so each payload is delivered once; remaining entries stay for the next poll.

Parameters:
  - key (string): Key passed to plugin_data_subscribe
  - maxItems (integer): Max entries to drain (1-10000, default 200)

tools.name: plugin_data_unsubscribe
tools.title: Unsubscribe from plugin data
tools.description:
Stops retaining payloads for a key and discards anything still queued for it.

Parameters:
  - key (string): Key passed to plugin_data_subscribe
